title: Functions [call & ret]
description:
## Functions in Assembly
You've been using labels and jumps. Functions are just labels with a convention:

- `call label` - pushes return address, jumps to label
- `ret` - pops return address, jumps back

Arguments go in registers (in order):
`rdi`, `rsi`, `rdx`, `rcx`, `r8`, `r9`

Return value goes in `rax`.

```asm
add_nums:
    mov rax, rdi
    add rax, rsi
    ret

_start:
    mov rdi, 5
    mov rsi, 3
    call add_nums
    ; rax is now 8
```

`call` is just `push` the next instruction's address + `jmp`. `ret` is just `pop` + `jmp`. That's it.


---
## Assignment:
LHINX needs a memory calculator. Write a function called `calc_mem` that takes the number of banks in `rdi` and multiplies by 512 (stored in the function). Call it with 4 banks.
starterCode:
section .data
    msg db "Memory calculated. Memory = "
    len equ $ - msg
    newline db 10

section .bss
    buffer resb 20

section .text
    global _start

; ===================================
; DO NOT MODIFY BELOW 
; ===================================
print_num:
    mov rsi, buffer + 19
    mov byte [rsi], 10
    mov rcx, 1
    mov rbx, 10
.loop:
    xor rdx, rdx
    div rbx
    add dl, '0'
    dec rsi
    mov [rsi], dl
    inc rcx
    cmp rax, 0
    jne .loop
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rdx, rcx
    syscall
    ret
; ===================================
; DO NOT MODIFY ABOVE
; ===================================

calc_mem:
    ; multiply rdi by 512, return in rax
    ret

_start:
    ; call here
    ; ===================================
    ; DO NOT MODIFY BELOW - prints result
    ; ===================================
    push rax
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, msg
    mov rdx, len
    syscall
    ; print the number
    pop rax
    call print_num

    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hint: Inside calc_mem, move rdi into rax, then use `imul rax, 512` or `shl rax, 9` (shift left by 9 = multiply by 512).
